method: Static semantic review of existing authoritative claim copies, evidence/voice plan, and effective assembly payloads. No fresh source-language retrieval or database query; source anchors/hashes are inherited locators, not newly verified here.
finding: A schema-compatible group label alone cannot resolve speaker/reporter roles, competing alternatives, or narrative-subject versus authority distinctions.

rows.statement_en: One interpretation identifies al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise; the cited reports describe its precious banks and bed, pleasant soil, and exceptionally sweet and white water.

staged_voice.originating_voice_name: Prophetic reports transmitted from Anas and Ibn Umar

staged_evidence.attributed_authority_name: Prophetic reports transmitted from Anas and Ibn Umar
staged_evidence.content_summary: One interpretation identifies al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise; the cited reports describe its precious banks and bed, pleasant soil, and exceptionally sweet and white water. Arabic anchor: الأول أنه نهر في الجنة ... عن ابن عمر ... حافتاه من ذهب ... ومجراه على الدر والياقوت.

source.evidence_anchor_ar: الأول أنه نهر في الجنة ... عن ابن عمر ... حافتاه من ذهب ... ومجراه على الدر والياقوت

rows.required_action: Separate report origins and transmission roles; do not treat Anas and Ibn Umar as joint authors of every descriptive detail.

rows.statement_en: A second interpretation identifies al-Kawthar with the Prophet's pool at the gathering; the cited report connects the promised river's abundant good with a pool visited by the community.

staged_evidence.content_summary: A second interpretation identifies al-Kawthar with the Prophet's pool at the gathering; the cited report connects the promised river's abundant good with a pool visited by the community. Arabic anchor: الثاني أنه حوض النبي ... قاله عطاء ... عليه خير كثير هو حوض ترد عليه أمتي.

source.evidence_anchor_ar: الثاني أنه حوض النبي ... قاله عطاء ... عليه خير كثير هو حوض ترد عليه أمتي

rows.required_action: Separate Ata's interpretation from the report transmitted from Anas; link each evidence span to its supported subclaim.

rows.statement_en: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and Yaman ibn Ri'ab identify al-Kawthar as the abundance of companions, the community, and followers.

staged_voice.originating_voice_name: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and Yaman ibn Ri'ab

staged_evidence.attributed_authority_name: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and Yaman ibn Ri'ab
staged_evidence.content_summary: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and Yaman ibn Ri'ab identify al-Kawthar as the abundance of companions, the community, and followers. Arabic anchor: السابع : هو كثرة الأصحاب والأمة والأشياع ; قاله أبو بكر بن عياش ويمان بن رئاب.

source.evidence_anchor_ar: السابع : هو كثرة الأصحاب والأمة والأشياع ; قاله أبو بكر بن عياش ويمان بن رئاب

rows.required_action: Candidate for grouped evidence with two distinct named voice records, not one concatenated originating person; retain one shared commentary witness.

rows.statement_en: The command to pray is variously explained as the obligatory prayer, the festival prayer on the Day of Sacrifice, and the dawn prayer at Muzdalifa; the sacrifice command is correspondingly linked with the rite, including slaughter after prayer.

staged_voice.originating_voice_name: al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas; Qatada, Ata, Ikrima; Anas; Said ibn Jubayr

staged_evidence.attributed_authority_name: al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas; Qatada, Ata, Ikrima; Anas; Said ibn Jubayr
staged_evidence.content_summary: The command to pray is variously explained as the obligatory prayer, the festival prayer on the Day of Sacrifice, and the dawn prayer at Muzdalifa; the sacrifice command is correspondingly linked with the rite, including slaughter after prayer. Arabic anchor: أقم الصلاة المفروضة ... صلاة العيد ويوم النحر ... صلاة الصبح المفروضة بجمع ... وانحر البدن بمنى.

source.evidence_anchor_ar: أقم الصلاة المفروضة ... صلاة العيد ويوم النحر ... صلاة الصبح المفروضة بجمع ... وانحر البدن بمنى

rows.required_action: Split obligatory, festival, and Muzdalifa readings with precise authority-to-reading links; preserve associated sacrifice qualifications.

rows.statement_en: Malik is reported as favoring the prayer of the Day of Sacrifice followed by the sacrifice, while acknowledging that he had received no transmitted statement on the verse.

staged_voice.originating_voice_name: Malik as reported by Ibn al-Arabi

staged_evidence.attributed_authority_name: Malik as reported by Ibn al-Arabi
staged_evidence.content_summary: Malik is reported as favoring the prayer of the Day of Sacrifice followed by the sacrifice, while acknowledging that he had received no transmitted statement on the verse. Arabic anchor: أما مالك فقال ما سمعت فيه شيئا ... والذي يقع في نفسي ... صلاة يوم النحر ... والنحر بعدها.

source.evidence_anchor_ar: أما مالك فقال ما سمعت فيه شيئا ... والذي يقع في نفسي ... صلاة يوم النحر ... والنحر بعدها

rows.required_action: Staged statement attributes the view to Malik while voice metadata also names Ibn al-Arabi as reporter. Do not map the entire string to one person or a co-originating group. Preserve Malik's no-transmitted-statement qualification.

rows.statement_en: Competing non-slaughter readings connect wanhar with placing the right hand over the left at the upper chest, raising the hands in prayer, or facing the qibla with the chest; these are retained as attributed alternatives.

rows.statement_en: Other reports identify Abu Jahl, Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, or the hostile Quraysh context involving Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and another explanation treats the hostile group itself as cut off after claiming Muhammad had separated from them.
